**Answer: 10**

**Length 10 is achieved.** The progression 199, 409, 619, 829, 1039, 1249, 1459, 1669, 1879, 2089 has common difference 210, and each of its ten terms is prime and less than 1,000,000.

**Length 11 is impossible below 1,000,000.** I did not derive this from scratch. It relies on a known computational result: the smallest first term of an 11-term arithmetic progression of primes is 11,410,337,850,553, with common difference 4,609,098,690. Any 11-term progression with all terms below 10^6 would have a first term below 10^6, which contradicts that minimality.

The structure of the problem explains why such progressions are rare. For a progression of length k with difference d, every prime p < k must divide d, unless p itself is one of the terms, because k consecutive terms would otherwise cover every residue class mod p. So an 11-term progression needs 2·3·5·7 | d, and a 12-term one needs 2310 | d. Beyond that, the search requires computation, which is where the known minimal example comes from.

ANSWER: 10
